As the Head of Central Robot Operations, you will lead the central operations organization that powers autonomous robot delivery at scale. Acting as the operational command center for the business, you will build the capabilities, mechanisms, and teams that enable safe, reliable, and efficient robot operations across every market.

You will own the operating model spanning Remote Assistance, Mapping Operations, Market Expansion, Infrastructure, Strategy & Operations, Policy & Demos, and Program Management etc. This leader will establish the systems, governance, and operational excellence needed to scale autonomous operations from a handful of cities to a global network, partnering closely with Engineering, Product, Safety, Hardware, Autonomy, Legal, Public Policy, and Market Operations.

What You Will Do

Build and Scale Central Robot Operations

  • Define the long-term operating model, organizational structure, and roadmap for Central Robot Operations.
  • Build scalable mechanisms, operating standards, and governance that enable reliable robot operations across all markets.
  • Lead a high-performing organization spanning operations, analytics, expansion, mapping, infrastructure, and program management.

Own Remote Assistance Operations

  • Lead the 24/7 Remote Assistance organization responsible for supporting autonomous robots requiring human intervention.
  • Define response-time SLAs, workforce planning, staffing models, scheduling, and escalation protocols.
  • Develop monitoring, telemetry, and operational dashboards that provide real-time visibility into fleet health.
  • Partner with Engineering and Product to analyze intervention data, eliminate recurring failure modes, and continuously reduce human intervention rates.

Lead Mapping Operations

  • Own the operational lifecycle of geospatial assets including HD maps, geofences, routing data, and points of interest.
  • Establish mapping quality standards, QA mechanisms, refresh cycles, and operational readiness processes for new launches.
  • Balance mapping accuracy with launch velocity while managing internal and external mapping partners.

Drive Geographic Expansion

  • Develop the playbook for launching new cities, campuses, and operating zones.
  • Lead market assessment, regulatory readiness, operational planning, and launch governance.
  • Build repeatable launch mechanisms that enable rapid, high-quality expansion across multiple geographies.
  • Coordinate cross-functional readiness reviews prior to every market launch.

Own Market Infrastructure

  • Lead strategy and execution for hubs, depots, charging infrastructure, parking locations, maintenance facilities, and operational footprint.
  • Drive capacity planning, infrastructure utilization, vendor management, and cost optimization.
  • Ensure operational infrastructure scales ahead of demand while maintaining service reliability.

Lead Strategy & Operations

  • Build the planning, analytics, governance, and reporting engine for Robot Operations.
  • Define KPIs, operating metrics, executive dashboards, forecasting models, and business review mechanisms.
  • Lead annual planning, OKRs, operational reviews, and cross-functional governance rhythms.
  • Translate operation al data into strategic recommendations for executive leadership.

Own Policy, Regulatory Engagement & Demonstrations

  • Partner with Public Policy and Legal teams to support permits, regulatory engagement, compliance initiatives, and government relationships.
  • Lead operational readiness for demonstrations involving customers, regulators, investors, media, and strategic partners.
  • Represent Operations during executive briefings and external engagements.

Lead Program Management

  • Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO) for Robot Operations.
  • Drive execution across multiple cross-functional workstreams through disciplined planning, dependency management, risk mitigation, and governance.
  • Establish operating cadences including weekly reviews, launch readiness reviews, retrospectives, and executive reporting.

We are looking for a creative, data-driven Compensation Specialist to join our team. As a Compensation Specialist, you will contribute to the development and implementation of our compensation approach. You will collaborate with team members to develop analytics tools, automate legacy processes, and help build the future of our compensation strategy. The ideal candidate is enthusiastic, hardworking, and thrives on building business focused solutions through data.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Evolve Compensation Strategy: Help us redefine and evolve how we believe about base, variable, and equity compensation structures
  • Advanced Analytics: Apply quantitative and qualitative analysis to identify problems, develop hypotheses, and recommend data-backed solutions for compensation programs and processes
  • Data Visualization & Modeling: Build and develop dynamic dashboards and analytic models to provide actionable business insights and interpret market or internal trends
  • Drive Automation: Streamline and automate monthly, quarterly, and annual compensation reporting and analysis using modern data tools and AI workflows
  • Market Benchmarking: Conduct global market benchmarking, assess peer groups, and ensure consistent market pricing practices while maintaining internal equity.
  • Storytelling with Data: Provide sophisticated compensation recommendations, clearly building data driven insights while tying it back to overall comp strategy

Who You Are:

  • Bachelor’s degree, preferably in a quantitative-focused major (e.g., Finance, Data Analytics, Statistics, Economics)
  • A minimum of 3+ years of experience in business analytics, finance or a related field in a fast-growing environment
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel (complex formulas, VBA, Power Query)
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable insights
  • Unmatched attention to detail; ensuring numbers are accurate & delivered on time to key partners
  • High learning agility, flexibility, and quantitative problem-solving skills



Bonus Points:

  • Consulting, Project Management or Analytics experience
  • Experience building interactive / replicable dashboards using Tableau, Power BI, or other advanced analytic platforms
  • Familiarity with Python, R, or SQL for data manipulation and automating repetitive workflows.

Strong planning, organizational, and project management skills

  • Demonstrated experience developing and implementing scalable, repeatable processes backed by detailed ongoing documentation

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

Benefits and Growth:

  • Generous and competitive benefits package
  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)
  • Continuous career development opportunities 
  • Product training to develop understanding of our product and space
  • Best in breed onboarding
  • Internal mentor and buddy program cross-departmentally
  • Friendly and inclusive workplace culture

Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.

 

Datadog offers a competitive salary and equity package. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, Datadog offers a wide range of best in class, comprehensive and inclusive employee benefits for this role including healthcare, dental, parental planning, and mental health benefits, a 401(k) plan and match, paid time off, fitness reimbursements, and a discounted employee stock purchase plan.

jobs.title: Fraud Strategy Associate
jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Operations at Brex

Operations is the backbone of Brex’s mission to power businesses through our Intelligent Finance Platform. We own credit, fraud, money movement, and payments, protecting our customers and our company. From product operations that ensure flawless launches to scalable systems that drive innovation and precision, we operate at the intersection of product, design, engineering, and customer success. If you want to work at the heart of the business, Operations is where you belong.

What you'll do

As a Fraud Strategy Associate, you’ll own the end-to-end integrity of Brex’s fraud and risk ecosystem across credit, deposit, and card payment rails. You'll find patterns, trace root causes, and build the detection logic, automations, and reporting that keep fraud in check without adding friction for customers. You’ll design your own solutions, see fraud across every product vertical, and partner with Risk, Data Science, Engineering, and Product to build prevention into the product itself. 

Where you'll work

This role will be based in our Seattle office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities

Strategic Analysis & Detection

  • Data Mining: Use SQL and Python to mine large-scale data, and apply LLM-based tools to detect and automate the identification of fraudulent patterns across credit, deposit, and card payment rails.
  • Vendor and Rule Optimization: Design and refine automated detection logic to proactively mitigate risk while maintaining a frictionless experience for legitimate customers.
  • Emerging Threat Intelligence: Stay ahead of industry trends and regulatory shifts to rapidly deploy new defensive strategies against novel fraud vectors.

Operational Excellence & Process Ownership

  • Workflow Architecture: optimize the internal processes for fraud investigations, ensuring operational discipline, case visibility, and high-fidelity documentation.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the strategic bridge between Risk Leadership, Analytics, Data Science, Engineering, and Product teams to integrate fraud-prevention infrastructure into the core product lifecycle.
  • Tooling & Infrastructure: Define and manage the technical requirements for internal AI-driven tools and third-party risk-reduction platforms.

Metrics, Reporting & Performance

  • KPI Management: Define and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) such as false positive rates, fraud capture rates, and operational turnaround times.
  • Executive Dashboards: Build and maintain scalable reporting suites to provide real-time visibility into fraud exposure and program effectiveness for senior stakeholders.
  • Impact Assessment: Conduct deep-dive post-mortems on fraud incidents to quantify financial impact and recommend structural process improvements.

Requirements

  • Industry Experience: 3+ years of experience in fraud strategy, risk operations, or data-driven business operations within a financial services or high-growth fintech environment.
  • Technical Mastery: Capable with SQL and/or Python for data wrangling, statistical modeling, and automation.
  • Operational Mindset: Proven ability to build scalable processes and manage complex project

jobs.title: Product Engagement Manager, User Operations
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Support team is central to ensuring that our customers' experience with our products is nothing short of exceptional. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Product Engagement Manager on the User Operations team, you will lead a team of Product Engagement Specialists responsible for ensuring smooth, successful product launches across internal and external teams. You’ll be the glue connecting product teams and support operations, equipping teams with the tools and knowledge needed to support new product rollouts. You’ll build scalable feedback loops that capture the voice of the user and translate insights into actionable product improvements, and ensure that frontline teams have the knowledge and skills to deliver accurate, delightful customer interactions at scale. We’re looking for someone who thrives at the intersection of product management, team enablement, and customer advocacy, and who enjoys working cross-functionally in a fast-paced, evolving environment. This person will manage the day-to-day work while also helping architect the systems needed to scale it. The successful candidate will be a leader-coach who can lead a small team while continuing to perform individual contributor work. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Lead a team coordinating product launches across internal and external teams, ensuring seamless execution and support readiness. - Set the team’s strategy and priorities, translate them into clear goals and quality standards, and allocate capacity to deliver against them. - Build a high-performing team through ongoing coaching, feedback, development, and performance management. - Build out a Voice of the User program with scalable feedback loops between support, Product, and Engineering pre and post launch, so customer insights inform product development and strategy. - Advocate for users by representing their needs and pain points in product and engineering discussions. - Partner with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Operations to align on launch goals and timelines. - Monitor post-launch performance and gather support data to assess product impact and inform improvements. - Document and standardize launch procedures to make them repeatable and scalable. - Identify launch risks and propose solutions that minimize disruption to customers. - Report on feedback-loop performance, including key insights, trends, and recommendations for the product roadmap. jobs.title: Asset Compliance Program Lead, Hardware
jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Central Procurement – Hardware Operations team is building scalable, AI-enabled operating foundations for a rapidly growing hardware footprint. We help the business move quickly while maintaining the data quality and controls needed to manage financial and operational risk responsibly. As OpenAI scales across R&D, new-product introduction, manufacturing, and third-party custody models, we are building the foundations to absorb complexity without adding unnecessary friction. That means establishing practical standards, strengthening discipline where it matters, using AI thoughtfully, and continuously improving how teams manage hardware operations. About the Role We are hiring an Asset Compliance Program Lead to establish the cross-business framework that gives OpenAI reliable lifecycle visibility over hardware-related financial assets and capital equipment. You will define the controls, systems roadmap, and evidence practices needed to manage those assets within OpenAI’s financial-control scope. This is a senior individual-contributor role in Central Procurement – Hardware Operations within Finance. Distinct from sourcing and transaction execution, you will partner with hardware business units, Accounting, Financial Risk Management, Procurement, contract manufacturers, and other third-party custodians to deploy practical operating mechanisms. These mechanisms will connect how assets are purchased, built, received, moved, held, verified, and retired with the ownership, data, reporting, and evidence needed for financial governance. The role covers those assets regardless of location or custody, including manufacturing equipment and tooling, supplier- and contract-manufacturer-held assets, leased assets, and other third-party-held equipment. You will stay close to the operational details—how assets move, where records diverge, which controls are not working, and where evidence is incomplete—and use that view to strengthen processes, accountability, and systems without compromising speed or flexibility. In this role, you will: - Design and scale the end-to-end asset-compliance operating model across acquisition and capitalization, custody and location tracking, transfers, lifecycle events, inventory and verification, impairment or retirement, and audit-evidence retention. - Define the authoritative asset record and systems roadmap, connecting requests, contracts, purchase orders, invoices, receiving, inventory data, physical custody, transfers, and financial records. - Establish clear ownership and control points across OpenAI teams, suppliers, contract manufacturers, logistics providers, and other third-party custodians. - Build lifecycle reconciliations and a scalable verification model across multiple internal and third-party sites, using risk-based inventories, sample testing, attestations, and corrective-action tracking to identify missing records, ownership or location gaps, unrecorded transfers, unresolved exceptions, and incomplete audit evidence. - Establish an initial baseline of asset exposure and control gaps, then prioritize remediation based on financial, operational, custody, and reporting risk. - Identify recurring issues and use process, system, workflow, automation, and AI-enabled improvements to prevent repeat problems and improve the stakeholder experience. - Shape policy, standards, and governance improvements by bringing operational evidence, implementation insight, and risk findings to the appropriate decision-makers. - Define executive reporting on asset completeness, control performance, audit readiness, remediation progress, and emerging risks. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy to define the right questions, build decision-ready insights, and influence Director and VP-level decisions on strategy, capacity, and investment for one of HubSpot’s most important segments.

Partner Development Team Manager, Japan

About HubSpot

HubSpot is a leading customer relationship management (CRM) platform designed to help companies scale and grow. Our mission is to empower tens of thousands of customers worldwide by providing them with the marketing, sales, and customer success software they need to not just grow, but to grow better.

At HubSpot, we live by our HEART values: Humble, Empathetic, Adaptable, Remarkable, and Transparent. We are seeking a Partner Development Team Manager to lead our dynamic team in Japan. This is a crucial leadership role within an expanding region, offering a unique opportunity to shape the foundations of our Partner Development organization.

As the PDM Manager, you will be instrumental in developing and evolving our partner ecosystem, with a strategic focus on the Upmarket space and driving partner-sourced business. You will be responsible for hiring, coaching, and leading a team of Partner Development Managers (PDMs) in a fast-paced environment. We are looking for a passionate and experienced leader who can build a high-performing team, foster a culture of continuous learning, and inspire both your team and our partners towards a collective vision.

This role is based in our Tokyo office area, with the expectation of coming into the office on a regular basis.

  • Lead and Inspire: Guide and manage the Partner Development team to exceed quarterly MBOs and monthly milestones, focusing on driving partner-sourced revenue, increasing revenue retention, and improving the selling rate.

  • Build and Recruit: Take responsibility for maintaining headcount by actively recruiting, selecting, and training new Partner Development Managers to attract and retain top talent.

  • Partner Leadership: You must have over five years of experience in a partner leadership position where you have demonstrably built and expanded a partner ecosystem (5+ years)

.

  • Experience supporting complex, multi-product partnership or commercialization motions that go beyond traditional media sales.

  • Familiarity with emerging commerce trends—such as retail media network

jobs.title: Manager, Enterprise Collections
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

We are seeking an experienced and strategic Manager II, Enterprise Collections to lead our Enterprise Collections organization, part of the broader Order to Cash function. As Manager II, Collections, you will drive collections performance for a portfolio of Samsara's enterprise customers, partnering closely with Sales, Customer Success, Legal, and Finance to support timely cash collection while delivering a strong customer experience. You'll lead and develop your team, manage escalations, and help scale the operating model through process improvement, automation, and adherence to strong governance (including SOX and policy compliance).

This role is ideal for a people-focused, detail-oriented operational leader who thrives in fast-paced, cross-functional environments.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except Alaska, Austin Metro, Boulder Metro, California, Chicago Metro, Connecticut, Dallas Metro, Denver Metro, Houston Metro, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, Seattle Metro, and Washington, D.C.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You're energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Own collections performance (aging, past-due reduction, dispute resolution velocity) for your team(s)' portfolio of enterprise accounts, balancing cash outcomes with customer experience.
  • Provide guidance and support for your team's development, including coaching and performance management for collections analysts and specialists.
  • Lead strategic initiatives to meet collections targets for one or more teams, and collaborate with senior leadership to align your team's collections strategies with broader OTC and enterprise goals.
  • Manage escalations and customer communication on complex accounts, navigating sensitive situations with sound judgment and professionalism.
  • Partner cross-functionally (Sales, Legal, Deal Desk, CS, FinSys, Treasury) to resolve complex invoicing/contract/payment issues and remove blockers to payment.
  • Drive and implement process improvements and automation (tools, workflows, reporting) to improve collections efficiency and the customer experience.
  • Participate in periodic reviews of OTC policies and SOX controls with senior leadership, and ensure your team's practices remain compliant and up to date.
  • Represent OTC/Collections in cross-functional initiatives.
  • Champion and role model Samsara's cultural principle

You will partner with Business Development, Product, Sales, Legal, Finance, and operational accounting teams to evaluate proposed contract terms and product offerings, explain their accounting and financial statement implications, and help stakeholders assess alternatives.

If you are driven to solve exhilarating challenges and have a bias toward action in the face of change, you will be empowered to make a real impact here, with a sharp and passionate team at your back. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can’t wait to meet you.

Location: Remote (US) — core hours estimated 9:00 AM–2:00 PM PT Mon–Thu, 9:00 AM–12:00 PM PT Fri 

About the Role

Our web marketing team runs several parallel workstreams: SEO/AEO, CRO, and quarterly web launches — supported by specialists and cross-functional partners. During a planned leave of absence, execution of each workstream is covered by existing team members. What this role owns is the connective tissue: the meeting rhythm, the follow-ups, and the cross-team communication that keep web marketing coordinated and moving.

This is a process-and-communication role managing high velocity workstreams across teams and aligning resourcing and helping leadership make decisions to keep the roadmap on schedule and on scope. You'll keep the moving pieces together so the team can stay focused on the work itself.

What You'll Own

Run the operating rhythm. Facilitate the weekly SEO/AEO/CRO meeting and keep web team standup mechanics tight: agendas, notes, and action tracking. Attend internal engineering, AEO/SEO, and web meetings and capture the requests and decisions landing on the web team. Sit on agency calls and assist with roadmap and follow ups and action items. 

Keep the roadmap visible. Assemble the written web updates broadcast to cross-functional stakeholders (reviewed by the web team lead before distribution) and help prioritize incoming work with input from workstream owners. 

Groom the backlogs. Keep the AEO/SEO and CRO backlogs current: mark items done, capture new requests for triage, and flag when runway is getting thin.

Track and chase. Follow up on action items across workstreams so nothing silently stalls.

Escalate with judgment. Spot blockers and route them to the right owner: execution questions to the web team lead, program decisions to the program owner. Deliver a weekly one-page status report to leadership so they have visibility without extra meetings. Act as the connective issue across a variety of marketing calls actively identifying which items are related for the web team and will need resourcing or prioritization. 

Support launch coordination. Keep the quarterly web launch checklist moving (owners, dates, dependencies) and partner with BizOps on timeline and strategy alignment, including occasional support materials such as slides.

Who You Are

  • 4+ years of experience as a marketing program manager or similar, with exposure to web or digital marketing, ideally in B2B SaaS. 
    • Web and demand generation experience a plus. 
  • Strong meeting facilitator who runs tight, productive sessions and leaves a clear paper trail
  • Excellent written communicator, especially in status updates and stakeholder summaries

We’re looking for a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to shape how businesses experience Afterpay and Cash App, from their first touch with us to becoming long-term partners. Your programs will turn prospects into merchants, get new merchants set up and transacting quickly, and give established merchants what they need to grow. jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About the Brand and Communications Team

Brand & Communications shapes how the world understands Affirm and how Affirm shows up in it. We meet people where perception forms: in culture, in the press, across our owned and paid channels, and inside the company. We aim to make our work compound over time, moving at the speed of culture while holding a high bar for craft and clarity. Our job across comms, brand, creative, and social is to make Affirm a brand people trust and are proud to choose.

About the Role

Affirm's model only works when consumers succeed. No late fees. The full cost, known before you commit. A balance that ends.

Many people don't know that. Pay-over-time products are treated as interchangeable, and the revolving credit card is treated as the responsible default. We want to change this dynamic and evolve thinking and beliefs around what consumer-friendly credit can and should be as it modernizes.

The timing is the opportunity. Credit is being rewritten right now, in regulation, in coverage, and in how people talk about debt. The beliefs that settle over the next few years will shape the decades that follow.

This role focuses on the people who shape what the public understands about credit, the ones creating the coverage and content that drives the conversation.

You know who covers what, who matters beyond their outlet’s size, which newsletter a Hill staffer reads before the front page. And you know how to proactively build an argument that travels. The policymakers, regulators, and advocates who set the terms will use it, and the most skeptical reporter will want to write it.

You won’t be doing it alone. You’ll collaborate with colleagues who own the narrative you’re carrying, the research behind it, and the versions of this story told to consumers, merchants, and investors. You’ll also partner closely with a policy team that owns our government relationships and the positions we take. And because this story has to build across audiences and surfaces, you’ll help shape the broader brand and comms strategy rather than only drawing from it.

This story lives at the nexus of New York City and Washington, DC, so you can be based in either with regular time in the other.

What You'll Do

  • Develop the strategy and run the campaign. Decide what we’re trying to change, with whom, and in what order. Set the sequence, pick the moments, and know what each one is supposed to do. Shift the dynamic from an idea we’re explaining to language other people naturally use.

  • Shape what becomes news. Be in the conversations where people are deciding what to cover and what counts as news, weaving Affirm into them rather than reacting to them.

  • Build the proof. Help shape original consumer research and third-party data into evidence that lets people outside Affirm make the argument correctly and persuasively without us in the room.

  • Build the media bench. Earn the trust of a focused group of reporters, columnists, editors, producers, podcasters, and independent writers who shape consumer finance and policy conversations, and become the source they come back to, including on stories that aren’t about us.

  • Partner on outside voices. Work with our public affairs and government relations team to build lasting relationships with consumer advocates, academics, and credit experts, starting with listening rather than endorsement requests. Design the dinners, briefings, and roundtables where the right people meet each other and the argument gets pressure-tested in person.

  • Put our perspective where decisions get made. Prepare executives and credible outside spokespeople for the moments that matter, from op-eds to panels and interviews, and work with public affairs so the arguments and themes we care about reach policymakers, regulators, and the people who advise them.

  • Know whether it is working. Track whether the argument is actually showing up: in how reporters frame the category, in the language advocates and policymakers use, in earned sentiment. Bring the honest read, including when a tactic is visible but not moving anything.

What We Look For

  • Campaign mindset: You think in arcs rather than announcements, built around the forces that actually shape the public conversation, and you know it’s landing when others start making the argument without you.

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

Airbnb's Business Technology (Biztech) organization sits at the heart of how we scale our internal operations to match the pace and ambition of our products. Within Biztech, the Finance Accounting Platform team owns the core finance accounting platform — the system that records, processes, and reports the financial lifecycle of every product Airbnb offers to the world. This is a senior finance systems product role: you are the product owner for the platform, its roadmap, and its controls.

As a Senior Platform Manager on this team, you will be embedded in a rich, cross-functional community spanning the full breadth of Airbnb's business. You'll partner daily with Product and Platform Managers across Payments, Trust, Guest & Host, Pricing, Insurance, Hotels, and Customer Service — as well as Finance stakeholders from Revenue Controllership, Treasury, Tax, Payments Legal, Consolidation, Collections, and Cash. You'll work closely with Data Engineers and Oracle Applications teams to bring platform solutions to life, and collaborate with FP&A and Business Unit teams who depend on the data your platform produces.
This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance, product, and engineering — often someone who started in accounting or audit and moved into finance systems or a techno-functional product management role — and who finds energy in being the connective tissue across a large, diverse, and highly capable community. Additionally, you bring in that broad perspective and proven track record of implementing platform solutions that scale to changing business needs

The Difference You Will Make:

You will be the strategic and operational owner of the finance accounting platform — the single point of accountability for shaping how it evolves to support Airbnb's growing portfolio of product offerings. Your impact will be felt across three dimensions:

Scaling the platform with Airbnb's ambitions — You will define and drive the long-term roadmap for the finance accounting platform, ensuring it can scale to support new product lines, geographies, and business models. You will own prioritization across a high-volume platform funnel — balancing competing requests with clarity and structured decision-making — and continuously identify opportunities to optimize platform performance and reliability.

Bringing new products to life on the accounting platform — Every time Airbnb launches or evolves a product, there is an accounting story that needs to be told accurately and at scale. You will lead that effort end-to-end — from initial accounting impact assessment through solution design, engineering alignment, UAT, release coordination, and production normalization — translating complex product changes into well-designed accounting workflows that record product lifecycle financials to Oracle FAH GL.

Strengthening the financial foundation — You will help define and refine data pipeline monitoring and SOX controls, support month-end close processes, and partner with Finance stakeholders to automate manual operational workflows. Your work will directly improve the accuracy, timeliness, and reliability of financial data that flows across Airbnb's Finance organization and beyond.

A Typical Day: 

No two days look the same, but here’s a window into what you might be doing:

  • Syncing with a cross-functional Product Manager from the Payments or Hotels team to understand an upcoming product change and assess its downstream accounting implications
  • Reviewing a product spec with Data Engineering to align on the implementation approach for a new accounting workflow feeding Oracle FAH
  • Running a UAT session with Revenue Controllership and Tax stakeholders to validate that a new product's financial lifecycle is being recorded

Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Marketing at Brex

Marketing tells the story of Brex to the world. From acquisition to activation, we translate product value into business results. What you’ll do

The Brex Marketing team is looking for an experienced Senior Marketing Operations Manager to architect and optimize our B2B sales-led and channel-driven GTM engine. This role will define and maintain the systems, processes, and operational rigor that align Marketing, SDR, Sales, and Partner teams.

We are looking for someone who is eager to design the future-state GTM tech stack—modernizing how leads flow, how insights are generated, and how operational workloads become more efficient through automation, AI, and agentic workflows. This person will champion operational excellence by improving lead management, automating revenue processes, increasing funnel velocity, and enabling more efficient cross-functional alignment.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our Salt Lake City office. jobs.title: Travel Operations Lead
jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE You'll join Ramp's travel team, which builds two products, Ramp Travel and Juno. Both integrate with a growing network of travel management company (TMC) partners. You'll be our expert on how those integrations work in practice: how content (search, booking and changes), payments, approvals, servicing and reporting flow between our products and each TMC. You'll own the operational side of each partnership, from the day it's signed through every customer that goes live on it. You'll work closely with engineering, our customer success managers, and the teams that sign new TMC partners and bring in customers through them, but you won't own those commercial relationships. Success means each new TMC goes live more efficiently than the last, mutual customers on each TMC go live faster and more smoothly over time as your playbooks improve, and the TMC servicing experience for Ramp and Juno travelers is seamless and delightful. The travel team is small and building quickly across both products, so everyone works beyond the edges of their role. Alongside your core work, you'll help wherever the team needs it most. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Build and refine our playbook for standing up a new TMC partner, and work with engineering to take each new TMC from signed partnership to its first live mutual customer. - For each live TMC, build the playbook for adding mutual customers and new points of sale, including in new countries and regions. Support CSMs when a rollout needs TMC-specific setup. - Investigate with engineering when bookings, payments or data don't flow correctly, and see fixes through with the TMC. - Train TMC agents who service accounts through our dashboards. For TMCs that use their own tools, make sure our workflows fit theirs. - Create SOPs for TMC agents to ensure they deliver top tier support for travelers. - Keep TMC partners up to date on product changes that affect them, and answer their agents' questions. - Always get to the why behind a TMC ask and make sure that it’s the best path forward. Just because something is done a certain way doesn’t mean that it’s the right or only way. - Actively track and analyze data to manage and measure the quality of the travel support experience offered by our partners. - Join partner review calls to represent day-to-day operations. - Identify the steps in your playbooks that can be automated or built into the product, and work with product and engineering to make that happen. - Take on work beyond your core role, such as joining Juno's customer support rotation, where you'll see firsthand how our partner integrations shape the customer experience. WHAT YOU NEED - 5+ years in implementation, partner operations, technical consulting, or a similar partner- or customer-facing technical role, ideally in travel technology, SaaS or fintech. - Corporate travel domain experience, such as working at a TMC or with GDSs (Sabre, Amadeus, Travelport), NDC content, or travel mid- and back-office systems. - Technical fluency to troubleshoot integrations and data flows across systems and hold credible conversations with engineers. Engineering depth is not required. - Experience managing external partners or vendors, and working cross-functionally with customer success, product and engineering. - Strong written communication, including the ability to train others and explain technical issues to nontechnical audiences. - AI fluency as a daily habit. Ramp is a builder culture: if you don't instinctively reach for AI before doing things manually, this role will be a hard adjustment. - Thrives in ambiguity and fast-paced environments, with a bias toward action and a high level of ownership. NICE-TO-HAVES - Technical fluency with APIs, integrations, debugging, or data analysis, even if you do not write production code. - Experience in B2B SaaS, travel, fintech, or another operationally complex product. BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL) - Flexible PTO - Centralized home-office equipment ordering - Health and wellness stipend - Budget

We are seeking a creative, strategic, and results-driven Brand Campaign Manager to bring the NiCE brand to life in market. NiCE is redefining the future of customer experience through AI-powered, end-to-end service automation, and our brand plays a critical role in how enterprise and C-level audiences see us. In this high-visibility role, you will plan, build, and launch integrated brand campaigns that elevate awareness, strengthen preference, and reinforce our position as the AI leader in CX. You will turn our brand platform and messaging into compelling, multi-channel campaigns across paid, owned, and earned media, partnering closely with Creative and Design, Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Social, PR, and external agencies. The ideal candidate blends big-picture brand thinking with strong program management, is comfortable working across global teams, and uses data to measure and continuously improve brand impact.

How will you make an impact

Brand Campaign Strategy & Planning
Develop and own integrated brand campaign plans that translate the NiCE brand platform, positioning, and messaging into clear campaign objectives, audiences, and channel strategies.
Partner with brand, marketing, and business leaders to align campaign priorities with company goals, product launches, and key moments such as major industry events and NiCE flagship events.

Campaign Execution & Creative Development
Lead end-to-end campaign execution from briefing through launch and optimization, across channels including digital and social, paid media, out-of-home, video, web, events, and thought leadership.
Write clear creative briefs and work closely with Creative and Design teams and external agencies to develop on-brand concepts, assets, and messaging that resonate with enterprise and C-level audiences.
Ensure every campaign touchpoint reflects NiCE brand standards, visual identity, and tone of voice.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Activation
Collaborate with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Field Marketing, Social, PR, and Analyst Relations to ensure consistent messaging and coordinated campaign activation across regions.
Equip regional and field teams with campaign toolkits and guidance so brand campaigns can be localized and amplified in market.
Support internal brand activation and employee advocacy programs that engage NiCErs as brand ambassadors.

Measurement, Budget & Operational Excellence
Define campaign KPIs and track performance, including reach, impressions, engagement, share of voice, brand awareness, and contribution to pipeline, sharing insights and recommendations with marketing leadership.
Manage campaign budgets, timelines, and resources to deliver strong return on investment.
Manage agency and vendor relationships, including scopes of work, deliverables, quality, and budget tracking.
Use AI tools and data insights to speed up campaign development, test new ideas, and continuously improve campaign effectiveness.

  • Excellent program and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple campaigns, deadlines, and stakeholders at the same time.
  • Analytical mindset with experience defining KPIs, measuring campaign performance, and turning data into actionable insights.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence across global, cross-functional teams.
  • Resiliency and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, complex, and ever-changing environment.

jobs.title: Research Engineer, AI for Chip Design
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI develops models that can reason through complex problems and hardware designed for the demands of advanced AI. AI for Chips connects these efforts: applying increasingly capable AI systems to the work of semiconductor engineering. Our goal is to help engineers develop better chips and shorten design cycles. This work brings research, model training, and hardware expertise together to build tools that engineers can use on real designs, with correctness and measurable performance at the center. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a Research Engineer to help OpenAI models solve chip-design problems through reinforcement learning, tool use, and evaluation. You’ll own experiments from the initial idea through implementation and analysis. That means building environments and evaluations, running training, investigating failures, and using the results to decide what to try next. You’ll also build the software needed to make those experiments reliable and reproducible. We value strong coding fundamentals, careful experimental judgment, and the ability to make progress independently. Prior chip-design experience is helpful, but you can learn the domain alongside the team’s hardware specialists. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Build RL environments and evaluations for tasks such as RTL generation, design verification, and physical design optimization. - Develop and test approaches that help models use chip-design tools and improve power, performance, and area while preserving correctness. - Design experiments, establish baselines, and measure whether improvements hold up on new tasks and designs. - Investigate failures across model behavior, rewards, evaluation tools, and experiment infrastructure. - Improve iteration speed through better tooling, faster evaluations, and proxy rewards that reflect the outcomes we care about. - Turn successful experiments into reusable research code and training workflows, working closely with researchers and engineers. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Have strong programming and debugging skills and a track record of turning technical ideas into working software. - Experience with reinforcement learning, model evaluations, post-training, or other applied ML research. - Experience building tool-using agents, reward functions, or automated evaluation systems. - Can form clear hypotheses, design useful experiments, and distinguish meaningful results from noise or evaluation errors. - Work independently on ambiguous problems and make practical decisions about what to build or test next. - Stay close to the implementation and can explain what you built, what failed, and what you learned. - Communicate progress clearly and collaborate well with people across research, software, and hardware. - Care about developing safe, beneficial AI. Join Anthropic's Customer Success team as an Munich based Customer Success Manager as we pioneer the future of enterprise AI adoption. You'll be a pioneer - helping to build regional processes, establishing new customer relationships, and representing Anthropic's brand in a high-growth market. At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

We’re looking for a Head of Internal Controls to join Gusto’s Finance, BizOps & Strategy team. This leader will partner with accounting and technical leaders to build and scale a forward-thinking internal controls environment that supports Gusto’s growth and operational maturity.

As the Head of Internal Controls, you will lead Gusto’s controls program across business process controls and IT controls. The scope includes the proprietary and third-party systems supporting Gusto’s payroll, health benefits, retirement, and other financial products.

Join our team...

GoDaddy Corporate Domains (GCD) is looking to hire an experienced, talented Client Success Manager with strong project management and domain management skills. The successful candidate will interact directly with GCD staff and clients to ensure a successful client experience through a variety of responsibilities that all contribute to supporting GCD clients. The successful candidate will be involved in the day-to-day management of corporate client domain portfolios, working with third-party domain management partners, creating internal and external reports, and other items which will ensure the client experience is as positive as possible through all facets of interaction with GCD.

We are looking for an individual with strong communication skills that has an interest in being part of a fast-moving and growing company focused on working with some of the most well-known companies in the world to manage their digital assets. It is of critical importance that you’re committed to working internally and externally so that GCD clients are the most delighted and loyal in the industry.

 

What you'll get to do...

  • Working with GCD Client Success Managers (CSM’s) and third parties in the day-to-day management of GCD domain names including domain registrations, transfers, updates, and other operations as needed.
  • Interacting directly with GCD clients in support of CSM’s as needed to ensure clients have redundancy in their support.
  • Assisting GCD CSM’s with technical issues including DNS issues, SSL Cert questions, and issues occurring at third-party domain management partners.
  • Working with other internal GCD staff to create, operationalize and review domain management reports which will provide different views into the operation of the business.
  • Interacting with other internal groups to support the successful operation of the business including, but not limited to, finance, sales, marketing, and legal.
  • Liaise with technical staff as needed to report and resolve any reported client technical issues.
  • Be able to take complex information and communicate with internal and external parties in a manner that is straightforward and easily digestible.

 

 Your experience should include...

  • 4+ years experience in the domain name industry, preferably in an account management or operations role.
  • 2+ years in an account management or client success role, preferably at a software-as-a-service company.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong technical skills with an understanding of DNS.
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage deadlines and work well under pressure.
  • Ability to work to a high degree of accuracy and great attention to detail.
  • High energy, a self-starting personality that works well in a start-up, fast-paced environment.
  • Intermediate, or higher, level skills in Microsoft Excel.

 

We encourage you to apply even if your experience or skillset doesn’t align perfectly with every requirement. We value a wide range of backgrounds and transferable skills, and we are excited to support learning and growth
.

Our mission is to give our customers the tools, insights, and people to transform their ideas and personal initiative into success.

jobs.location: San Francisco, CA • New York, NY
jobs.description:
Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

Figma is hiring a Corporate Communications Manager to help us set a new standard for corporate communications at a public company. Successful candidates will go beyond setting strategy to help define a new model for how public companies communicate. This person will partner across the company — finance, investor relations, legal, brand, product and design — to mine and tell stories that drive conversation across audiences, formats and channels. 

This role calls for range. You should be as comfortable in a spreadsheet as you are on X/Twitter. You’re capable of crafting campaigns around quarterly earnings and cultural moments. You can quickly learn and translate complex topics for a broader audience without dumbing it down. You embrace ambiguity, are collaborative by default, and are energized by the opportunity to build something new. 

This is a full time role that can be held from our San Francisco or New York hub.

What you’ll do at Figma:

  • Help define and drive Figma’s corporate storytelling strategy end-to-end, from narrative development to execution across channels
  • Move beyond traditional PR to create integrated campaigns that cut through across media, owned platforms and executive communications
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to translate business momentum into clear, compelling stories and campaigns
  • Work closely with executives to shape narratives that resonate with business and financial audiences, from briefings to thought leadership
  • Identify and develop breakthrough story angles that position Figma at the center of key industry, market and cultural conversations
  • Stay close to the news cycle and broader zeitgeist while proactively creating opportunities that put Figma ahead of it
  • Continue to grow your scope and influence as the company scales

We’d love to hear from you if you have:

  • 7+ years of experience in in-house communications
  • A track record of building and scaling communications programs from the ground up
  • Strong business and cultural fluency, with the ability to translate complexity into clear, engaging narratives and pitches
  • Experience operating in fast-paced environments where direction isn’t always defined—and comfort creating it
  • Demonstrated experience crafting a point of view on storytelling that goes beyond conventional PR approaches

While not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

  • An understanding of product design, software development and/or cloud-native applications.
  • Experience navigating and explaining business concepts and issues with fluidity.
At Figma, one of our values is Grow as you go. We believe in hiring smart, curious people who are excited to learn and develop their skills. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager - LPM Foundations
jobs.description:
About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The payments landscape is changing rapidly, with businesses and their customers relying on a growing mix of local payment methods, cards, wallets, bank payments, buy now, pay later, and digital currencies. Stripe’s Local Payment Methods (LPM) business is one of our fastest-growing payments businesses.

LPM Foundations builds and operates the core platform that enables Stripe’s Local Payment Method teams—and their first- and third-party developers—to build, integrate, and run high-quality payment methods at scale. We turn complex product integrations into reusable, self-service platform capabilities so teams can launch new LPMs faster and reduce the long-term cost of operating them.

This is a payments role with a platform and AI focus. We are building the foundations, interfaces, and workflows that let product and engineering teams use AI effectively to accelerate development, improve decisions, and scale reliable payments experiences globally.

What you’ll do

As an Engineering Manager, you will lead the LPM Foundations team at the center of Stripe’s long-term payments growth strategy. You will translate regional and strategic priorities into a focused platform roadmap, shape technical direction with your team, and drive execution across the systems behind critical payment flows. You will be deeply involved in engineering and design, while coaching, mentoring, and creating the conditions for an effective, inclusive team.

Responsibilities

  • Set the vision and roadmap for platform capabilities that help LPM teams build, integrate, and operate payment methods at scale.
  • Lead engineers in designing and delivering reliable, self-service foundations that simplify complex integrations and speed up launches.
  • Build an AI-first engineering organization: develop the platform hooks and working practices that enable agentic development and help teams use AI to improve execution and product-engineering decisions.
  • Partner closely with customers, engineering, product, partnerships, legal, operations, and other stakeholders to align priorities and deliver end-to-end outcomes.
  • Drive clear technical and architectural decisions with staff engineers, balancing reliability, extensibility, velocity, and regional payments complexity.
  • Lead and improve the team’s operating processes so it can execute effectively and engage well with the rest of Stripe.
  • Recruit, develop, and retain great engineers; support their growth and help build a challenging, supportive, and inclusive team culture.
  • Contribute to engineering-wide initiatives as a member of Stripe’s engineering management team.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • At least 5 years of experience managing teams that shipped high-quality products.
  • An entrepreneurial mindset and comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy and responsibility in an ambiguous environment.
  • A track record of recruiting, developing, and building great engineering teams.
  • The ability to work effectively across functions, think rigorously, communicate clearly, and make or coordinate hard decisions and trade-offs.
  • Technical acumen to partner with staff engineers on architecture and technical strategy.
  • Experience creating a healthy and inclusive work environment that is both challenging and supportive.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience building platforms, developer products, or large-scale distributed systems.
  • Experience applying AI to software development, engineering workflows, or product delivery, with strong judgment about where it creates durable value.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for leadership, users, and company-wide audiences.
  • A strong quantitative and analytical background.
  • Experience leading fully remote or distributed teams.

DoorDash is looking for an experienced Manager, Tax Technology to lead the tax platform and business projects of our growing Tax Team, with an emphasis on new integrations — new verticals, new merchants/partnerships, and new product launches. This role sits at the intersection of tax, product, engineering, and the Vertex Center of Excellence — turning business and tax requirements into configured, tested, live capabilities and working with the offshore implementation team delivering that work day to day. 

 

As DoorDash continues to grow across new verticals and markets, we are looking for a candidate who combines indirect tax knowledge with the ability to translate business and tax requirements into clear functional system requirements, lead cross-functional delivery, and own the delivery of new tax platform features on both the in-house and third party tax engines.

About the Role

You will report to the Senior Manager of the Tax Calculation Platform & Mx Operations and lead tax platform and business projects on the DoorDash platform. You will partner closely with Tax Engineering, Tax Advisory & Planning (TAP), Tax Product, and other stakeholders — gathering business and tax requirements, translating them into tax-system functional requirements for configuration, testing and cutover, and reviewing Technical Design Documents (TDDs) to provide functional tax expertise back to Tax Engineering.

The primary focus of this position is end-to-end delivery of tax features, new-vertical / new-merchant or partnership / new-product launches, and legislative changes on the DoorDash platform, grounded in US sales and use tax, Canada GST/HST/PST, and Australia and New Zealand GST, across food and beverage and retail tax context, with an understanding of how data flows from upstream systems through the tax engine to downstream reporting. Rather than handing off requirements to the Vertex Center of Excellence team, you will apply your own Vertex knowledge to help influence the functional design and determine the specific Vertex configuration a solution requires. This position may work remotely within the US, but will be based on the East Coast to accommodate EMEA time zones and meetings with global stakeholders. 

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Lead tax platform and business projects on the DoorDash platform, including new vertical launches, business and enterprise merchant launches, new product launches, and legislative changes.

  • Define testing requirements and oversee test validations across unit, integration, E2E, shadow, and post-launch phases.
  • Trace tax-relevant data from upstream systems through Vertex to downstream reporting, and flag gaps or risks.

  • Partner closely with US and Mexico based peers and offshore team members on the same pillar — sharing workload, coordinating coverage across time zones, and supporting knowledge transfer on complex initiatives.

We’re excited about you because…

  • You have 6+ years of indirect tax or indirect tax technology experience.
  • You are well versed in US sales and use tax, with experience across Canada GST/HST/PST and Australia and New Zealand GST, and food and beverage and retail tax context.
  • Hands-on experience implementing or configuring Vertex O Series, and ability to review Vertex configurations and testing documentation and provide feedback.

  • You can translate business and tax requirements into functional system requirements and review technical and functional design documents.
  • Direct engagement with engineering teams on tax system technical and functional design, product development, with working knowledge of the end to end tax platform launch processes.

jobs.title: Business SOX Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara is looking for an experienced manager to lead SOX business process compliance and help keep the trust in our financial reporting as strong as the business we’re building. As part of our SOX Compliance team, you’ll help oversee and strengthen Samsara’s global control environment, protecting the accuracy of our financial reporting and keeping us compliant as we scale. You’ll partner closely with IT and business process owners to design and implement controls, spot gaps early, and drive remediation to the finish line. We’re looking for someone who takes real ownership. You bring deep, hands-on SOX expertise, a track record of delivering projects reliably, and the confidence to run with complex work independently. If you take pride in being the person others count on to get it done right, we’d love to meet you.

This is a remote position open to candidates based in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best. 

In this role, you will: 

  • Develop, lead, and execute periodic financial risk assessments, materiality calculations, and scoping of the SOX program
  • Develop and deliver training to SOX control owners, including process documentation, testing methodology, management review controls, and controls over Information Produced by the Entity (IPE).
  • Conduct walkthroughs across all business process areas and work with business process owners to ensure timely review and updates to the control documentation
  • Collaborate cross functionally to design leading edge practices with a financial compliance mindset across several complex business process areas.

  • Ownership of control deficiency evaluation, aggregation analysis as well as development and execution of related remediation plans.
  • Help drive the SOX AI transformation strategy by identifying high-value opportunities, implementing AI-enabled solutions, and driving adoption and new ways of working across the global SOX organization.
  • Provide reporting to business leaders on program status, health, and effectiveness of the business process control environment

Our virtual accounts enable international consumers and businesses to easily access, store, and spend US dollars. Our payouts infrastructure enables platforms to disburse USD to anyone globally. We believe many trillions of dollars will move and settle through stablecoin payment rails. Bridge is pulling this future forward.

We have a small team of people who have previously built financial infrastructure at some of the world's leading companies (Coinbase, Stripe, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, Airbnb), and each and every one of them chose Bridge because they fundamentally believe that stablecoins will be a critical piece of financial infrastructure that improves global money movement.

jobs.title: Manager, Lease Accounting
jobs.description:
About the Team

The DoorDash Lease Accounting team ensures DoorDash’s lease portfolio is reported accurately and on time under ASC 842. This requires deep technical accounting review and careful interpretation of complex, often ambiguous lease arrangements. As the portfolio grows in size and complexity, we continue to strengthen our processes to keep pace with the business.

About the Role

You will report to the Senior Accounting Manager on our Lease Accounting team. As the Lease Accounting Manager, you will be a key technical expert on ASC 842, ensuring DoorDash’s leases are accounted for accurately as the business grows. This role is built for someone who takes ownership, stays ahead of the work, and works closely with partners across functions. Success means well-supported conclusions and dependable reporting each period, with the opportunity to apply your expertise to increasingly complex leases.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Review lease abstractions against new lease agreements and lease modifications to ensure accurate classification and recognition of each lease in accordance with ASC 842.
  • Perform detailed accounting analysis of complex lease arrangements and unique scenarios that go beyond standard treatment, documenting conclusions and supporting analysis.
  • Perform lease monthly close activities including journal entries, account reconciliations, and flux analysis
  • Own lease financial reporting deliverables, including cash flows, rollforwards, and disclosures.
  • Partner closely with Real Estate, Lease Administration and other cross-functional teams to understand lease activity early and keep the accounting accurate and timely.
  • Proactively identify and lead process improvements and automation initiatives to reduce manual work and improve the accuracy and efficiency of processes.
  • Maintain lease SOX controls and support both internal and external audit requests.

We’re excited about you because…

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, or a related field, and/or equivalent work experience.
  • 6+ years accounting experience, including in-depth experience applying US GAAP lease accounting (ASC 842), which is essential to this role.
  • Proven experience reviewing lease agreements, interpreting lease terms, and assessing their financial implications to determine the appropriate accounting treatment.
  • Ownership mindset and proactiveness, with a track record of managing multiple deliverables and following them through to completion on close timelines.
  • Strong cross-functional partnership and communication skills to work effectively with internal and external partners.
  • Close attention to detail and demonstrated problem-solving skills.

We expect this position to be filled by 01/03/2027

Compensation

The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

jobs.description:
About the Team

DoorDash is one of the world's most trusted on-demand logistics platforms. The Global Safety and Security team exists to keep it that way, protecting our people, property, operations, brand, and reputation across all our markets. We manage risk and create value through agility, technology, and a people-first approach. Our DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt brands now span more than 40 countries, dozens of offices, and tens of thousands of employees. Protective Services focuses specifically on the safety of our executives, their families, and the operations that support them. Its detection engineering function brings together enterprise, marketplace, open-source, and physical security signals to identify threats that do not fit within a traditional SOC boundary. This role builds the detection capabilities that turn those signals into timely, actionable information for Protective Services.

We are hiring a Senior Detection Engineer to build and improve the technical capabilities Protective Services uses to identify threats to protected individuals. You will develop detections, pipelines, enrichment, and automation across enterprise security telemetry, marketplace signals, open-source information, and physical security systems. This detection problem extends beyond conventional cybersecurity alerts. Relevant indicators may appear across identities, endpoints, cloud environments, support interactions, marketplace activity, access-control events, or unstructured online content. You will determine how to combine those signals, distinguish meaningful escalation from noise, and directly investigate resulting activity alongside Protective Services partners. That proximity to active cases grounds engineering decisions in real investigative needs and reveals opportunities to improve fidelity, automate friction, and reduce time to action. This is a hands-on security engineering role. You will work in code, queries, data pipelines, detection repositories, and production systems; carry detections from hypothesis through deployment and optimization; and use operational outcomes to improve coverage and quality.   • Build, test, deploy, and operate detection-as-code pipelines that support reliable detection at DoorDash’s scale
  • Integrate enterprise telemetry, marketplace activity, physical security events, OSINT, support interactions, and other external signals into detections tailored to protective use cases
  • Work with structured and unstructured data, applying rules, statistical methods, machine learning, and LLM-backed techniques where they measurably improve detection and investigation
  • Develop and maintain automation and agentic tooling that improve detection efficacy, streamline investigative workflows, and reduce repetitive work
  • Own the detection lifecycle from hypothesis and data validation through deployment, tuning, measurement, and retirement; maintain detection repositories and use case libraries
  • Conduct technical triage and investigations, correlate signals across sources, assess confidence and scope, and help Protective Services partners determine the appropriate response
  • Follow detections through investigation, response, and mitigation, using case outcomes, false positives, and missed indicators to improve detection coverage and quality

  • Create and maintain engineering standards, testing practices, and documentation that improve service consistency and reliability
  • Mentor and uplevel other engineers through technical reviews, knowledge sharing, and hands-on collaboration
  • Participate in our on-call rotation and support significant protective cases
